segments.he: הַצַּדִּיקִים מַכְנִיסִים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לִצְעק בְּכָל פַּעַם אֶל ה'
segments.en: For instance, when one knows that tzitzis is efficacious for breaking the desire for niuf [licentiousness], and for meriting the counsel of the Tzaddikim, and for complete faith, and for prayer, and for the Land of Israel, and for performing miracles — then one can certainly compose many extensive prayers about tzitzis. For each person knows within himself how far he is from the rectification of the bris, and how the desire for licentiousness overcomes him — which is the core battle of every person — and how much salvation and compassion he needs to attain the true counsel, which is the counsel of the Tzaddikim. About all these he can pour out his speech in prayer, making from this Torah teaching prayers that lay bare all that is in his heart. And similarly from other Torah teachings — from one teaching about the mezuzah that subdues the desire for money and nullifies the torment of livelihood pressures and enables contentment with one's portion — how many heartfelt supplications one can pour forth until one pours one's heart like water before Hashem.

segments.he: וְזֶה בְּחִינַת הַנּוּנִין הֲפוּכִין שֶׁבְּקַפִּיטְיל ק"ז בִּתְהִלִּים בְּמִזְמוֹר הוֹדוּ. שֶׁמְּדַבֵּר מִכָּל הַגָּלֻיּוֹת שֶׁנָּפְלוּ כְּנֶסֶת יִשְִׂרָאֵל בָּהֶם שֶׁתִּקּוּנָם עַל יְדֵי בְּחִינַת הַנּוּן שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ. שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת הַצַּדִּיקֵי אֱמֶת שֶׁבְּכָל דּוֹר שֶׁמַּכְנִיסִין בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל. לִצְעק בְּכָל פַּעַם לַה' וּלְהוֹדוֹת לוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל חֲסָדָיו וְנִפְלְאוֹתָיו שֶׁעוֹשֶׂה עִמָּנוּ בְּכָל עֵת בְּתוֹךְ עמֶק מְרִירוּת הַצָּרוֹת בְּגוּף וְנֶפֶשׁ וּמָמוֹן וְכוּ'.
segments.en: Thus the essential completeness of prayer — making prayers from Torah teachings — comes from the Torah innovations described. And this is the aspect of Simchas Beis HaShoayvah [the Water-Drawing celebration]: "You shall draw water with joy from the wellsprings of salvation" [Yeshayahu 12:3] — accepting new Torah teachings [ulpan chadash], the innovations drawn from the ancient-hidden wisdom, through which one can make prayers from Torah teachings. And through these one can pour one's heart like water before Hashem — each person according to the pain he knows in his own heart, how far he is from Hashem and into what bad desires, confusions, and sins he has fallen — all this he can find within these prayers he makes from the Torah teachings, pouring out his speech before Him in compassion and supplication about all of them, as a son who pours his heart before his father. Until one merits to pour one's heart like water. This is the aspect of "wellsprings of salvation" — for this path is the wellsprings of salvation, flowing from a never-ending spring that can save everyone, whoever they are, even in their current state.

segments.he: וְכֵן לִצְעק וְלַחֲזר וְלִצְעק בְּחִינַת וַיִּצְעֲקוּ וַיִּצְעֲקוּ וְכוּ'.
segments.en: Through this path of making prayers from Torah teachings, one is never put to shame when returning to Hashem — no matter what one has done, no matter where one stands at this moment, each person knowing his own situation. Even so, through this path — which flows from the gleaming of Moshiach who is drawing near to come speedily in our days — we can all, however we are, return to Hashem blessed be He. For all our repentance and our hope and our expectation before Hashem depends solely on prayer: on how we yearn and beseech and implore Hashem to return us to Him and to help us and save us with His great might and His wondrous kindnesses, to fulfill the entire Torah from this moment on. Therefore now there is no reason for us to collapse in our minds and cease praying to return to Hashem because our deeds are not as they should be — for is this not precisely what we are asking of Hashem: that He help us to rectify our deeds? And in this we can always be occupied, until He has mercy upon us from Heaven to fulfill our request. And truly, whoever is steadfast in this path, to multiply hisbodidus and make prayers from Torah teachings and multiply such prayers always — whatever else may be — will certainly have a good end. And in the end, end of all ends, he will certainly return to Hashem in truth, as we have understood from his holy mouth many times.

segments.he: כַּמּוּבָא בָּזֶה הַרְבֵּה בִּדְבָרֵינוּ. (שָׁם אוֹת סו):
segments.en: And this is what the verse cries out: "How long will you turn away, O wayward daughter? For Hashem has created something new on the earth — a woman shall encompass a man" [Yirmeyahu 31:22] — which Rashi explains in reference to teshuvah: tis'chamkin means "you hide from Me, ashamed to return to Me because of your ways. Behold, something new has been created on the earth — the female shall pursue the male..." This refers to nekavah tesovev gaver — the feminine encompassing the masculine — which is the aspect of making prayers from Torah teachings, as explained above. For Torah is the aspect of the masculine and prayer is the aspect of the feminine — Torah She'biksav and Torah She'b'al Peh — and when prayer is fashioned from Torah teachings, this is the feminine encompassing the masculine. Through this path one need never be ashamed to return to Hashem at any time, whatever the situation. For His compassion is inexhaustible, and at every moment one can come with prayer and supplication to ask Him to draw one near from this point forward.
